library(gt)

# APA style ####
gt_apastyle <- function(gt_table, font.size=12) {
  gt_table  |> 
    gt::opt_table_lines(extent = "none") %>%
    gt::tab_options(
      heading.border.bottom.width = 2,
      heading.border.bottom.color = "black",
      heading.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      table.border.top.color = "black",
      table.border.top.style = "solid",
      table.border.top.width = 2,  
      table_body.hlines.color = "white",
      table_body.border.top.color = "black",
      table_body.border.top.style = "solid",
      table_body.border.top.width = 2,
      heading.title.font.size = font.size,
      table.font.size = font.size,
      heading.subtitle.font.size = font.size,
      table_body.border.bottom.color = "black",
      table_body.border.bottom.width = 2,
      table_body.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
      column_labels.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = 1,
      latex.use_longtable = FALSE
    ) |> 
      gt::opt_table_font(font = "times")
}

Demographics

Gender

Code 
pool_coef <- function(with = "Age", component = "Demographic", category = "Demographic", name = with, unequalrange=FALSE) {
  rez <- data.frame()
  for(intero in vars_intero) {
    data <- data.frame() 
    for(dataset in alldata) {
      if (with %in% names(dataset)) {
        d <- dataset[c(with, intero, "Sample")]
        data <- rbind(data, d)
      }
    }
    
    
    # Make sure that min-max of "with" is the equal across all samples
    check <- summarize(data, 
                       min = min(!!sym(with), na.rm = TRUE),  
                       max = max(!!sym(with), na.rm = TRUE), .by = "Sample")
    if (with != "Gender" && (any(check$min != min(check$min)) || any(check$max != max(check$max)))) {
      if(unequalrange == FALSE) {
        print(check)
        stop(paste0("The range of '", with, "' is not equal across samples."))
      }
    }
    
    
    data <- standardize(data[complete.cases(data), ])

    if (with == "Gender") {
      data <- data[data$Gender != "Other",]
      data$Gender <- factor(data$Gender, levels = c("Male", "Female"))
      f <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~", with, " + (", with, "|Sample)"))
      f2 <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~", with, " + (1|Sample)"))
      f3 <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~ Sample * ", with))
    } else {
      f <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~", with, " + (", with, "|Sample)"))
      f2 <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~", with, " + (1|Sample)"))
      f3 <- as.formula(paste0(intero, "~ Sample / ", with))
    }
    
    # Mixed models
    control1 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl()
    control2 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(optimizer=optim, optArgs=list(method="BFGS"))
    m <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(f, data = data, control=control1)
    type <- "Full"
    if(!insight::is_converged(m) || is.nan(insight::get_statistic(m)$Statistic[2])) {
      m <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(f, data = data, control=control2)
      type <- "Full"
    }
    if(!insight::is_converged(m)  || is.nan(insight::get_statistic(m)$Statistic[2])) {
      m <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(f2, data = data, control=control1)
      type <- "Reduced"
    }
    if(!insight::is_converged(m) || is.nan(insight::get_statistic(m)$Statistic[2])) {
      m <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(f2, data = data, control=control2)
      type <- "Reduced"
    }
    
    # # Marginal
    # m <- lm(f3, data = data)
    # modelbased::estimate_slopes(m, trend = with)
    
    out <- parameters::parameters(m)[2, ] |> 
      select(r = Coefficient, CI_low, CI_high, p) |> 
      as.data.frame()
    out$var_Interoception <- intero
    out$var_Correlate <- with
    out$Category <- category
    out$Component <- component
    out$Type <- type
    out$Converged <- insight::is_converged(m)
    out$N <- nrow(data)
    out$k <- length(unique(data$Sample))
    rez <- rbind(rez, out)
    
  }
  rez$var_Correlate <- name
  rez
}

check_ranges <- function(var = "Neuroticism") {
  for(d in names(alldata)) {
    dataset <- alldata[[d]]
    if(!var %in% names(dataset)) next
    print(paste0(d, ": ", paste(round(range(dataset[[var]], na.rm=TRUE), 2), collapse = "-")))
  }
}

Average Correlations

  • BPQ - sf - Body perception questionnaire short form
  • BPQ - vsf - Body perception questionnaire very short form
  • BVAQ - Bermond–Vorst Alexithymia Questionnaire
  • MAIA-2 - Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness , Version-2
  • ICQ - Interocpetive Confusion Questionnaire
  • TAS - Toronto Alexithymia Scale
  • BAQ - Body awareness questionnaire
  • PHQ-2 - Patient Health Questionnaire 2 items on major depressive episodes
  • PHQ-4 - atient Health Questionnaire 4 items assessing anxiety and depression
  • PHQ-9 - Patient Health Questionnaire 9-Item Version assesses depressive symptoms
  • PHQ-15 - Patient Health Questionnaire 15-Item Version assesses Somatic symptom distress
  • GAD-2 - Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale 2 items on anxiety disorder
  • STAIT - State-Trait-Anxiety Inventory Trait subscale
  • FFMQ - Observation and Description subscales of the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire
  • NEOFFI - Neuroticism Neo Five-Factor Inventory Neuroticism subscale
  • BDI - The Beck Depression Inventory
  • BFI - Big Five inventory-10
  • ASQ - Autism-Spectrum Quotient
  • GCB - Generic Conspiracist Beliefs scale
  • IPIP6 - Mini International Personality Item Pool
  • PI - Primal Inventory 18 items and 99 items
  • PID5-sf - Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Short Form
  • SPQ-BRU - Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire, brief revised updated
  • LIE - Lying Profile Questionnaire

Sample sizes

Code 
nk <- data |>
  summarise(N = max(N), k = max(k), .by = c(Category, var_Correlate)) |>
  arrange(Category, desc(N))

# Range for the text and the table note
nk_range <- paste0(format(min(nk$N), big.mark = ","), "–", format(max(nk$N), big.mark = ","),
                   "; k = ", min(nk$k), "–", max(nk$k))

nk_table <- nk |>
  mutate(var_Correlate = str_replace(var_Correlate, "Boderline", "Borderline"),
         Category = fct_relevel(Category, "Demographics", "Interoception", "Mood", "Personality",
                                "Psychopathology and Neurodevelopmental Traits", "Beliefs")) |>
  # "Subscale - Questionnaire" -> two columns (labels without a questionnaire, e.g. "Gender (Female - Male)", stay whole)
  mutate(Questionnaire = replace_na(str_match(var_Correlate, " - ([^()]+)$")[, 2], ""),
         Subscale = str_remove(var_Correlate, " - [^()]+$"),
         .keep = "unused") |>
  arrange(Category, desc(N)) |>
  select(Category, Questionnaire, Subscale, N, k)

# Saved as data (rebuilt as a flextable in the manuscript's supplementary materials, Table S1)
saveRDS(nk_table, "figures/table3.rds")

nk_table |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Category") |>
  cols_move_to_start(c(Questionnaire, Subscale)) |>
  cols_label(Questionnaire = "Questionnaire", Subscale = "Dimension", N = "N", k = "k") |>
  fmt_integer(N) |>
  cols_align("left", c(Questionnaire, Subscale)) |>
  cols_align("center", c(N, k)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#FFF8E1"), locations = cells_body(rows = k == 1)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_row_groups()) |>
  tab_header(title = "Sample size per association") |>
  tab_footnote(paste0("Note. N = largest number of participants across the IAS outcomes; k = number of samples. ",
                      "Across all associations, N = ", nk_range, ". ",
                      "Shaded rows are based on a single sample (k = 1).")) |>
  gt_apastyle(font.size = 11)

p <- data |>
  mutate(sig = ifelse(p < .01, "p < .01", ifelse(p < .001, "p < .001", "N.S.")),
         dir = sign(r),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "CoughSneeze", "Cough/Sneeze"),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "HungryThirsty", "Hungry/Thirsty"),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "BruiseBlood", "Bruise/Blood sugar"),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "MusclesPain", "Muscles/Pain"),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "BreathingHeart", "Breathing/Heart"),
         var_Interoception = str_replace(var_Interoception, "UrinateDefecate", "Urinate/Defecate"),

Correlation Matrix Between Dimensions

Pooled correlations between the correlate dimensions most often measured together (the IAS is not included). For each pair of dimensions, correlations were computed within each sample measuring both (n ≥ 20) and pooled with a DerSimonian–Laird random-effects model on Fisher-z values. Questionnaire dimensions (not totals) are correlated.

Code 
core <- c(
  "MAIA_Noticing", "MAIA_NotDistracting", "MAIA_NotWorrying", "MAIA_AttentionReg", "MAIA_EmoAwareness",
  "MAIA_SelfReg", "MAIA_BodyListening", "MAIA_Trusting", "BPQ_BodyAwareness",
  "TAS_DIF", "TAS_DDF", "TAS_EOT", "ICQ", "IATS_Mean",
  "STAIT_Mean", "PHQ4_Anxiety", "PHQ9_Sum", "PHQ4_Depression", "Neuroticism")
# Other dimensions were only added if they shared at least two samples with most of these dimensions;
# autistic traits (ASQ, CATI, AQ-50) and the remaining measures overlap with them in one sample at most.

# Within-sample correlations for one pair of dimensions, pooled across samples (random effects, Fisher z)
pool_r <- function(a, b) {
  st <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(alldata), \(s) {
    x <- alldata[[s]]
    if (!all(c(a, b) %in% names(x))) return(NULL)
    d <- na.omit(data.frame(a = as.numeric(x[[a]]), b = as.numeric(x[[b]])))
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || sd(d$a) == 0 || sd(d$b) == 0) return(NULL)
    data.frame(sample = s, r = cor(d$a, d$b), n = nrow(d))
  }))
  if (is.null(st)) return(data.frame(z = NA, se = NA, k = 0, N = 0))
  z <- atanh(st$r); v <- 1 / (st$n - 3); w <- 1 / v
  zf <- sum(w * z) / sum(w); Q <- sum(w * (z - zf)^2); k <- nrow(st)
  tau2 <- if (k > 1) max(0, (Q - (k - 1)) / (sum(w) - sum(w^2) / sum(w))) else 0
  ws <- 1 / (v + tau2)
  data.frame(z = sum(ws * z) / sum(ws), se = sqrt(1 / sum(ws)), k = k, N = sum(st$n))
}

pairs_core <- t(combn(core, 2))
cormat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_core)), \(i) {
  cbind(var1 = pairs_core[i, 1], var2 = pairs_core[i, 2], pool_r(pairs_core[i, 1], pairs_core[i, 2]))
})) |>
  mutate(r = tanh(z), p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z / se)),
         stars = case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", p < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ ""))

lab <- c(Original = "IAS total", HungryThirsty = "IAS Hungry–Thirsty", MusclesPain = "IAS Muscles–Pain", WindBurp = "IAS Wind–Burp",
         UrinateDefecate = "IAS Urinate–Defecate", BreathingHeart = "IAS Breathing–Heart", BruiseBlood = "IAS Bruise–Blood sugar",
         CoughSneeze = "IAS Cough–Sneeze", MAIA_Noticing = "MAIA Noticing", MAIA_NotDistracting = "MAIA Not-Distracting",
         MAIA_NotWorrying = "MAIA Not-Worrying", MAIA_AttentionReg = "MAIA Attention Regulation", MAIA_EmoAwareness = "MAIA Emotional Awareness",
         MAIA_SelfReg = "MAIA Self-Regulation", MAIA_BodyListening = "MAIA Body Listening", MAIA_Trusting = "MAIA Trusting",
         BPQ_BodyAwareness = "BPQ Body Awareness", TAS_DIF = "TAS Difficulty Identifying", TAS_DDF = "TAS Difficulty Describing",
         TAS_EOT = "TAS Externally Oriented", ICQ = "ICQ Interoceptive Confusion", IATS_Mean = "IATS Attention",
         STAIT_Mean = "STAI-T Trait Anxiety", PHQ4_Anxiety = "PHQ-4 Anxiety", PHQ9_Sum = "PHQ-9 Depression",
         PHQ4_Depression = "PHQ-4 Depression", Neuroticism = "Neuroticism")
lv <- unname(lab[core])
fmt_r <- function(x) sub("^(-?)0[.]", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", x))

d_cor <- cormat |>
  mutate(v1 = factor(lab[var1], levels = lv), v2 = factor(lab[var2], levels = lv),
         label = ifelse(k == 0, "", paste0(fmt_r(r), stars, "\nk = ", k)))

p_cor <- ggplot(d_cor, aes(x = v1, y = v2)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = r), colour = "white") +
  geom_tile(data = filter(d_cor, k == 1), fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pooled r",
                       na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(lv[-1])) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = c(0.85, 0.75),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7.5)) +
  labs(caption = paste0("Each cell: pooled within-sample correlation (random-effects, Fisher z) and number of samples (k).\n",
                        "* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001; dashed outline = single sample (k = 1); grey = never measured in the same sample."))

Discussion

Benefits of the IAS: - Straightforward and sensation-centered items

Recommendations: - Remove Itch (redundant + issue in Chinese) - Use analog scales

Limitations: - Not much clear theorethical or empirical structure (small grouping of items) - Limited variability (clear mode at 4/5), very low prevalence of 5/5 responses. - Ambiguous items which grouping depends on the context (and its awareness) - E.g., heart beating fast, vomit when nauseaous - Few items for some modalities (e.g., 1 for heart) - Positive phrasing: benefits but also might exacerbate positivity bias (and thus unidimensionality)

Need for context-specific items (cross-modal when possible, i.e., cardioception, respiroception, etc.).

Neuroticism: effect unclear

Openness (driven by Wind/burp): effect of response bias
